1. Let φ' := covectorPullback n Q.symm φ, so φ'(v) = φ(Q⁻¹v_0, …, Q⁻¹v_{n−1}). Let dx^α := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (α j)) and ψ := Σ_α euclideanCovectorCoordinate φ' α • dx^α.

By wedge_kronecker only α = γ survives: its first conjunct at γ gives 1, and its second conjunct with I := α, J := γ ≠ α gives 0. So the coordinate is φ'(e_γ) (Finset.sum_eq_single). This is Step 2(a).
3. covector_ext gives φ' = ψ, the standard expansion of φ'. This is Step 2(b).
4. Q.symm (Q x) = x gives φ = covectorPullback n Q φ'. Linearity of covectorPullback n Q then gives φ = Σ_α φ'(e_α) • covectorPullback n Q dx^α.
5. SimonGMT covectorPullback_wedgeCovectors gives covectorPullback n Q dx^α = wedgeCovectors n (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)).comp Q) = Q^*dx^α. Moreover φ'(e_α) = φ(fun i => Q.symm (e_{α(i)})) by definition. This is the frozen conclusion. No case split on n or P is needed.

  intro P n Q φ
  classical
  set φ' : Covector (Eucl P) n := covectorPullback n (Q.symm : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl P) φ with hφ'
  have hstd : φ' = ∑ α : SimonMultiIndex n P,

    apply Submission.polyhedral_approx_pairing_covector_ext

        euclideanCovectorCoordinate φ' α • wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (α j)) :
          Covector (Eucl P) n) γ
        = ∑ α : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate φ' α *
            euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (α j))) γ := by
      simp only [euclideanCovectorCoordinate, ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply,
        ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    rw [hlin, Finset.sum_eq_single γ]
    · rw [(Submission.polyhedral_approx_pairing_wedge_kronecker P n γ).1, mul_one]
    · intro α _ hα
      rw [(Submission.polyhedral_approx_pairing_wedge_kronecker P n α).2 γ (Ne.symm hα), mul_zero]
    · intro h
      exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ γ) h
  have hφ : φ = covectorPullback n (Q : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl P) φ' := by
    ext v
    simp [hφ', covectorPullback_apply, Function.comp_def]
  conv_lhs => rw [hφ, hstd]
  rw [map_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun α _ => ?_
  rw [map_smul, covectorPullback_wedgeCovectors]

subproblems.title: Kronecker duality of coordinate wedges on increasing multi-indices (Simon 6.1.1–1.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 be the k-th standard basis vector of ℝ^P = Eucl P. For a strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P), let dx^I := dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n−1)} = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P). Then dx^I(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = 1. Moreover dx^I(e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}) = 0 for every J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I. In the project's notation: euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1, and euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0 for all J ≠ I.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : SimonMultiIndex n P), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) I = 1 ∧ ∀ J : SimonMultiIndex n P, J ≠ I → euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) J = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (Kronecker property) of the parent-supplied proof of rpn_covector_rotated_expansion (the expansion ω = Σ_α ω_α dx^α at the start of Simon's proof of Lemma 2.36, in the coordinates of Simon Ch. 6, §1), specialized to this exact statement with the details filled in. The statement is the accepted declaration Submission.polyhedral_approx_pairing_wedge_kronecker, reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 and x^k := EuclideanSpace.proj k, so x^k(y) = y_k for y ∈ E. For J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P write e_J := (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}). By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate ω J = ω(e_J) for every ω ∈ Covector E n. Fix I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P and put dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => x^{I(j)}). Every element of SimonMultiIndex n P is an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P, hence strictly increasing and injective.

1. (Matrix entries.) For a, b ∈ Fin P, x^a(e_b) is the a-th coordinate of EuclideanSpace.single b 1. It is 1 if a = b and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply).
2. (Determinant formula.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. By SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = dx^I(e_J) = det M_J, where M_J := Matrix.of (fun k l => x^{I(k)}(e_{J(l)})). By Step 1, (M_J)_{k,l} = 1 if I(k) = J(l) and (M_J)_{k,l} = 0 otherwise.
3. (First conjunct, J = I.) Since I is injective, I(k) = I(l) holds iff k = l. Hence (M_I)_{k,l} is 1 if k = l and 0 otherwise, so M_I is the identity matrix (Matrix.one_apply) and det M_I = 1 (Matrix.det_one). By Step 2, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1.
4. (A strictly increasing map is determined by its range.) Let J, J' ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with range J = range J' =: S. Fix k ∈ Fin n. Since J is strictly increasing and S = range J, the elements of S below J(k) are exactly J(0), …, J(k−1). So J(k) is an element of S with exactly k elements of S below it. Such an element is unique: if s < s' are both in S, then s lies below s' but not below s, so s' has strictly more elements of S below it than s. The same characterization holds for J'(k). Hence J(k) = J'(k) for every k, i.e. J = J'. (Mathlib: OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT.)
5. (A missing row index when J ≠ I.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I, and suppose for contradiction that every I(k) lies in range J. Then range I ⊆ range J. Both I and J are injective on Fin n, so both ranges have exactly n elements (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), and range J is finite. A subset of a finite set with at least as many elements equals that set (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). So range I = range J, and Step 4 gives I = J, contradicting J ≠ I. Hence there is k ∈ Fin n with I(k) ≠ J(l) for every l ∈ Fin n.
6. (Second conjunct, J ≠ I.) Take k from Step 5. By Step 2, (M_J)_{k,l} = 0 for every l ∈ Fin n, so row k of M_J is zero and det M_J = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero). By Step 2 again, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0. Since J ≠ I was arbitrary, the second conjunct holds. Together with Step 3, this proves the statement for all P, n and I.
7. (Degenerate sizes.) No case split is needed. For n = 0, M_I is the empty matrix. It equals the identity, so det M_I = 1. SimonMultiIndex 0 P has exactly one element, so the second conjunct is vacuous; Steps 4–5 also apply verbatim, since both ranges are empty. For n > P, SimonMultiIndex n P is empty and the statement is vacuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = det M_J with (M_J)_{k,l} = 1 if I(k) = J(l) and 0 otherwise (wedgeCovectors_apply_det and PiLp.single_apply).
J = I: injectivity of I makes M_I the identity matrix, so the coordinate is det 1 = 1.
J ≠ I: a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is determined by its range, and both ranges have n elements, so some I(k) lies outside range J.
Row k of M_J is then zero, so the coordinate is 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).

subproblems.title: An n-covector on ℝ^P is determined by its increasing-basis coordinates (Simon 6.1.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α, β ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) be n-covectors, i.e. continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n). For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Suppose α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = β(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), i.e. euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I, for every strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P). Then α = β.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α β : Covector (Eucl P) n), (∀ I : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I) → α = β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (standard expansion) of the parent-supplied proof of rpn_covector_rotated_expansion, specialized to this exact statement with the details filled in. That step shows that two alternating maps which agree on increasing tuples of standard basis vectors agree on all basis tuples (non-injective tuples by alternation, injective ones by sorting), hence everywhere (Module.Basis.ext_alternating). The statement is the accepted declaration Submission.polyhedral_approx_pairing_covector_ext, reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P write e_v := (e_{v(0)}, …, e_{v(n−1)}). Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis be the standard basis of E; then b k = e_k (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I = γ(e_I) for γ ∈ Covector E n and I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. Let f and g be the alternating maps underlying α and β (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap); f takes the same values as α, and g the same values as β.

1. (Reduction to alternating maps.) A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So it suffices to prove f = g.
2. (Reduction to injective basis tuples.) By Module.Basis.ext_alternating for the basis b, it suffices to prove f(e_v) = g(e_v) for every injective v : Fin n → Fin P. This is the extensionality step of the parent proof. Expanding every argument in the basis b, the multilinear maps f and g are determined by their values on all tuples e_v with v : Fin n → Fin P. If v is not injective, e_v has two equal entries, so f(e_v) = 0 = g(e_v) because f and g are alternating. Fix an injective v.
3. (Sorting.) Let σ := Tuple.sort v. It is a permutation of Fin n such that v ∘ σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). The map v ∘ σ is injective, as a composition of the injective maps σ and v, so it is strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective). Let I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (v ∘ σ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, so I(j) = v(σ(j)) for all j ∈ Fin n. (I is the increasing enumeration γ of range v from the parent proof, and v = I ∘ σ⁻¹.)
4. (Tuple identity.) e_v = e_I ∘ σ⁻¹, i.e. e_{v(i)} = e_{I(σ⁻¹(i))} for every i ∈ Fin n, because I(σ⁻¹(i)) = v(σ(σ⁻¹(i))) = v(i).
5. (Sign rule.) Let h be an alternating map with arguments indexed by Fin n, u : Fin n → E a tuple and τ a permutation of Fin n. Then h(u ∘ τ) = sign(τ) · h(u) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Take u := e_I and τ := σ⁻¹ and use Step 4. For γ ∈ {α, β} this gives γ(e_v) = sign(σ⁻¹) · γ(e_I) = sign(σ⁻¹) · euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I.
6. (Conclusion.) By hypothesis, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I. By Step 5, f(e_v) = α(e_v) = sign(σ⁻¹) · euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = sign(σ⁻¹) · euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I = β(e_v) = g(e_v). As v was an arbitrary injective tuple, Step 2 gives f = g, and Step 1 gives α = β.
7. (Degenerate sizes.) No case split is needed. For n = 0 the only tuple is the empty one. It is injective, σ is the identity and I is the empty embedding. For n > P there is no injective v : Fin n → Fin P, so the condition in Step 2 holds vacuously and α = β (both are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce α = β to equality of the underlying alternating maps on injective tuples of standard basis vectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective, Module.Basis.ext_alternating with the standard basis); non-injective tuples are killed by alternation.
Sort an injective v with σ := Tuple.sort v. Then I := v ∘ σ is strictly increasing, an element of SimonMultiIndex n P, and e_v = e_I ∘ σ⁻¹.
AlternatingMap.map_perm gives γ(e_v) = sign(σ⁻¹)·euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I for γ = α, β. The coordinate hypothesis then gives α(e_v) = β(e_v), hence α = β.
